documents.title: Accounting Standards & Principles
documents.summary: Core accounting standards, GAAP/IFRS principles, and financial reporting requirements
documents.body:
# Accounting Standards & Principles

## Overview

This document outlines the accounting standards and principles that govern financial reporting. All financial activities must comply with the applicable accounting framework (GAAP or IFRS depending on jurisdiction).

## Core Accounting Principles

### 1. Accrual Basis
Revenue is recognized when earned, not when cash is received. Expenses are recognized when incurred, not when paid.

### 2. Consistency Principle
Once an accounting method is chosen, it should be used consistently across reporting periods. Any changes must be disclosed with justification.

### 3. Going Concern
Financial statements are prepared assuming the business will continue operating indefinitely.

### 4. Materiality
All materially relevant information must be disclosed. An item is material if its omission or misstatement could influence economic decisions.

### 5. Prudence (Conservatism)
When uncertainty exists, choose the method that least overstates assets and income, and least understates liabilities and expenses.

### 6. Substance Over Form
Transactions should be recorded based on their economic substance, not merely their legal form.

## GAAP vs IFRS Comparison

| Aspect | GAAP | IFRS |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | Rules-based | Principles-based |
| Inventory costing | LIFO allowed | LIFO prohibited |
| Development costs | Expensed as incurred | Capitalized if criteria met |
| Revenue recognition | Detailed industry-specific guidance | Principles-based, fewer industry rules |
| Lease accounting | Operating vs finance leases | Single lessee model |
| Intangible assets | Revaluation not allowed | Revaluation allowed |
| Balance sheet | Current/non-current required | Current/non-current preferred but not required |

## Chart of Accounts Structure

### Standard Account Categories
1000-1999: Assets
  1100: Cash & Cash Equivalents
  1200: Accounts Receivable
  1300: Inventory
  1400: Prepaid Expenses
  1500: Property, Plant & Equipment
  1600: Intangible Assets

2000-2999: Liabilities
  2100: Accounts Payable
  2200: Accrued Liabilities
  2300: Deferred Revenue
  2400: Short-term Debt
  2500: Long-term Debt

3000-3999: Equity
  3100: Common Stock
  3200: Additional Paid-in Capital
  3300: Retained Earnings
  3400: Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income

4000-4999: Revenue
  4100: Product Revenue
  4200: Service Revenue
  4300: Other Income

5000-5999: Cost of Goods Sold
  5100: Direct Materials
  5200: Direct Labor
  5300: Manufacturing Overhead

6000-6999: Operating Expenses
  6100: Salaries & Wages
  6200: Rent & Facilities
  6300: Marketing & Sales
  6400: Research & Development
  6500: General & Administrative
  6600: Depreciation & Amortization

7000-7999: Other Income/Expenses
  7100: Interest Income
  7200: Interest Expense
  7300: Foreign Exchange Gains/Losses

8000-8999: Income Tax
  8100: Current Tax Expense
  8200: Deferred Tax Expense

## Revenue Recognition (ASC 606 / IFRS 15)

### Five-Step Model
1. **Identify the contract** with the customer
2. **Identify performance obligations** in the contract
3. **Determine the transaction price**
4. **Allocate the transaction price** to performance obligations
5. **Recognize revenue** when/as performance obligations are satisfied

### SaaS Revenue Recognition Example
- Monthly subscription: Recognize ratably over the subscription period
- Annual subscription (paid upfront): Defer revenue, recognize monthly
- Setup fees: Recognize over the expected customer relationship period
- Usage-based fees: Recognize as usage occurs

## Monthly Closing Checklist

### Day 1-3: Revenue & Receivables
- [ ] Record all invoices and credit memos
- [ ] Reconcile payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal, etc.)
- [ ] Review AR aging and follow up on overdue accounts
- [ ] Calculate and record bad debt allowance

### Day 3-5: Expenses & Payables
- [ ] Process and record all vendor invoices
- [ ] Reconcile corporate credit cards
- [ ] Accrue for any unrecorded expenses
- [ ] Review prepaid schedules and record amortization

### Day 5-7: Payroll & Benefits
- [ ] Record payroll journal entries
- [ ] Accrue for bonuses, commissions, and benefits
- [ ] Reconcile payroll tax liabilities

### Day 7-10: Fixed Assets & Intangibles
- [ ] Record depreciation and amortization
- [ ] Review asset additions and disposals
- [ ] Impairment review (quarterly)

### Day 10-12: Intercompany & Consolidation
- [ ] Record intercompany transactions
- [ ] Eliminate intercompany balances
- [ ] Currency translation adjustments

### Day 12-15: Review & Finalize
- [ ] Trial balance review
- [ ] Flux analysis (variance vs prior period and budget)
- [ ] Review by accounting manager
- [ ] Finalize and distribute financial statements

documents.title: Tax Compliance & Regulations
documents.summary: Tax compliance requirements, filing deadlines, and regulatory obligations
documents.body:
# Tax Compliance & Regulations

## Overview

This document covers tax compliance requirements, key deadlines, and regulatory obligations for the finance department. Staying compliant requires proactive monitoring of tax law changes across all jurisdictions where the company operates.

## Corporate Income Tax

### Federal Income Tax
| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Tax rate | 21% (US corporate flat rate) |
| Filing form | Form 1120 (US corporations) |
| Filing deadline | 15th day of 4th month after year-end (extensions available) |
| Estimated payments | Quarterly (15th of April, June, September, December) |
| Penalty for late filing | 5% per month up to 25% of unpaid tax |

### State Income Tax
| State | Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Delaware | 8.7% flat | No sales tax, franchise tax applies |
| California | 8.84% flat | Minimum $800 annual franchise tax |
| Texas | 0.375-0.75% | Gross receipts tax (no income tax) |
| New York | 6.5-7.25% | Based on income brackets |
| Nevada | 0% | No corporate income tax |

## Sales Tax / VAT

### US Sales Tax
- **Economic nexus**: Collect sales tax where the company has physical presence OR exceeds economic thresholds (varies by state, typically $100K-$500K in sales or 200+ transactions)
- **Registration**: Register in each state where nexus is established
- **Filing**: Monthly, quarterly, or annually depending on volume
- **Rates**: State + local = combined rate (typically 6-10%)

### EU VAT
- **Standard rate**: 17-27% depending on country
- **OSS (One Stop Shop)**: Simplified VAT filing for cross-border EU sales
- **Digital services**: Taxed in the customer's country (not the seller's)

### Digital Services Tax
- Several countries impose digital services tax on tech companies
- Rates range from 1.5% to 7.5% on digital service revenue
- UK: 2% on revenues exceeding 25M from UK users
- France: 3% on revenues exceeding 25M in France / 750M globally

## Payroll Taxes

| Tax | Employer Rate | Employee Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Social Security | 6.2% | 6.2% | Up to wage base ($160,200 in 2024) |
| Medicare | 1.45% | 1.45% | No wage base |
| Additional Medicare | - | 0.9% | On wages > $200K (single) |
| FUTA | 6.0% (0.6% net) | - | On first $7,000 per employee |
| SUTA | Varies by state | - | Rate depends on experience rating |

## International Tax Considerations

### Transfer Pricing
- Transactions between related entities must be at arm's length
- Penalties for non-compliance: 5-40% of adjustment amount

### Withholding Taxes
| Type | Typical Rate | Treaty Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dividends | 30% | 0-15% | Depends on treaty |
| Interest | 30% | 0-15% | Portfolio interest exemption |
| Royalties | 30% | 0-15% | Depends on treaty |

## Key Deadlines Calendar

| Date | Obligation | Jurisdiction |
|---|---|---|
| Jan 15 | Q4 estimated tax payment | US Federal |
| Jan 31 | W-2 and 1099 filing | US Federal |
| Mar 15 | Corporate tax return (calendar year) | US Federal |
| Apr 15 | Q1 estimated tax payment | US Federal |
| Jun 15 | Q2 estimated tax payment | US Federal |
| Sep 15 | Q3 estimated tax payment | US Federal |
| Dec 15 | Q4 estimated tax payment (corporate) | US Federal |

## Record Retention Requirements

| Record Type | Retention Period |
|---|---|
| Tax returns and supporting docs | 7 years after filing |
| Employment tax records | 4 years |
| Payroll records | 6 years |
| Accounts payable/receivable | 7 years |
| Contracts and agreements | 10 years after termination |
| Corporate records (charter, minutes) | Permanent |
| Property records (asset lifecycle) | Until disposal + 7 years |

documents.title: Financial Reporting & Analysis
documents.summary: Standards for financial reporting, management reporting, and financial analysis
documents.body:
# Financial Reporting & Analysis

## Overview

Financial reporting provides stakeholders with accurate, timely information about the company's financial performance and position. This document defines the standards for both external (GAAP/IFRS) and internal (management) reporting.

## External Financial Statements

### Balance Sheet (Statement of Financial Position)
Reports assets, liabilities, and equity at a point in time.

**Key Line Items:**

*Assets*
- Cash & Cash Equivalents
- Accounts Receivable (net of allowance)
- Prepaid Expenses
- Property, Plant & Equipment (net of depreciation)
- Intangible Assets (net of amortization)
- Goodwill

*Liabilities*
- Accounts Payable
- Accrued Expenses
- Deferred Revenue
- Short-term Debt
- Long-term Debt

*Equity*
- Common Stock & APIC
- Retained Earnings
- Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI)

### Income Statement (P&L)
Reports revenues, expenses, and profit over a period.

**Key Line Items:**
- Revenue (by segment: product, service, other)
- Cost of Revenue / COGS
- Gross Profit
- Operating Expenses (R&D, Sales & Marketing, G&A)
- Operating Income (EBIT)
- Interest Income/Expense
- Other Income/Expense
- Pre-tax Income
- Income Tax Expense
- Net Income

### Cash Flow Statement
Reports cash inflows and outflows by activity.

**Three Sections:**
1. **Operating Activities**: Cash from core business operations
2. **Investing Activities**: Cash from asset purchases/sales, acquisitions
3. **Financing Activities**: Cash from debt/equity issuance, dividends, buybacks

## Management Reporting

### Monthly Financial Package
Delivered by Day 15 of the following month:

1. **Executive Summary**: Key financial highlights and KPIs
2. **Income Statement**: Actual vs Budget vs Prior Year
3. **Balance Sheet**: Current period with variance analysis
4. **Cash Flow Statement**: Actual vs Forecast
5. **Revenue Analysis**: By product line, channel, and customer segment
6. **Expense Detail**: Major expense categories with variance explanations
7. **KPI Dashboard**: Key metrics (ARR, MRR, churn, CAC, LTV, etc.)
8. **Outlook**: Updated forecast for remaining quarters

### Key Financial KPIs

| KPI | Calculation | Target Range |
|---|---|---|
| Gross Margin | (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue | > 70% (SaaS), > 30% (product) |
| Operating Margin | EBIT / Revenue | > 15% (healthy) |
| Current Ratio | Current Assets / Current Liabilities | > 1.5 |
| DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) | (AR / Revenue) x 365 | < 45 days |
| Debt-to-Equity | Total Liabilities / Total Equity | < 1.0 |
| Revenue Growth | (Current Period / Prior Period - 1) x 100 | > 20% YoY |
| EBITDA Margin | EBITDA / Revenue | > 20% |

### Variance Analysis

When a line item deviates > 10% from budget/forecast, document:
1. **What happened**: Description of the variance
2. **Why**: Root cause (volume, price, mix, timing, one-time)
3. **Impact**: Quantitative effect on the business
4. **Action**: What management should do in response

## Reporting Cadence

| Report | Audience | Frequency | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly financial package | Management | Monthly | Day 15 |
| Quarterly financials | Board | Quarterly | Day 30 after quarter |
| Annual report | External stakeholders | Annually | 90 days after year-end |
| Board deck | Board of Directors | Quarterly | 7 days before board meeting |
| Tax returns | Tax authorities | Annually | Per filing deadline |

## Financial Systems & Tools

| System | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| ERP (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero) | General ledger, AP, AR, reporting | Accounting |
| Billing platform (Stripe, Chargebee) | Subscription billing and revenue recognition | Finance Ops |
| Expense management (Expensify, Concur) | Employee expense reporting | Accounting |
| FP&A tool | Budgeting, forecasting, modeling | FP&A |
| Audit management | Audit evidence collection | Controller |
| Tax compliance | Tax filing and compliance | Tax team |

documents.title: Compliance & Regulatory Requirements
documents.summary: Key compliance frameworks, regulatory requirements, and internal controls
documents.body:
# Compliance & Regulatory Requirements

## Overview

This document covers the key compliance frameworks, regulatory requirements, and internal controls applicable to the company. Compliance is a shared responsibility across the organization, coordinated by the compliance team.

## Compliance Framework Overview

| Framework | Scope | Required For | Applicability |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOC 1 (SSAE 18) | Financial reporting controls | Public companies, regulated industries | Annual audit |
| SOC 2 | Security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy | SaaS companies, enterprise customers | Annual audit |
| SOX | Internal controls over financial reporting | Public companies (US) | Annual certification |
| GDPR | Data protection and privacy | Companies with EU/UK customer data | Ongoing compliance |
| HIPAA | Healthcare data privacy | Healthcare companies or vendors | Ongoing compliance |
| PCI-DSS | Payment card data security | Companies processing card payments | Annual assessment |
| ISO 27001 | Information security management | Enterprise companies | Recertification every 3 years |

## Internal Controls Framework

### Control Categories

**Preventive Controls** (stop errors/fraud before they happen):
- Segregation of duties
- Authorization requirements
- Access controls
- Validation and verification

**Detective Controls** (identify errors/fraud after they happen):
- Reconciliations
- Reviews and approvals
- Monitoring and alerts
- Audit trails

### Key Financial Controls

| Control | Description | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| Bank reconciliation | Reconcile all bank accounts to GL | Daily/Monthly |
| AR reconciliation | Reconcile AR subledger to GL | Monthly |
| Revenue recognition review | Review revenue entries for compliance | Monthly |
| Expense approval | All expenses above threshold require approval | Per transaction |
| Journal entry approval | All JEs require review and approval | Per entry |
| Access review | Review system access rights | Quarterly |

## Segregation of Duties

### Incompatible Duties
The following duties should NEVER be performed by the same person:

| Duty | Incompatible With |
|---|---|
| Initiating a payment | Approving the payment |
| Creating a vendor | Approving invoices from that vendor |
| Recording cash receipts | Performing bank reconciliation |
| Preparing financial statements | Reviewing financial statements |
| Access to production data | Authorizing data changes |
| Writing checks | Signing checks |

## Audit Preparation

### External Audit Preparation
1. **Pre-audit meeting** (60 days before): Discuss scope, timeline, and requests
2. **PBC (Provided by Client) list**: Complete by 4 weeks before fieldwork
3. **Walkthroughs**: Demonstrate key processes and controls
4. **Testing**: Provide evidence for control effectiveness
5. **Closing meeting**: Review draft findings
6. **Final report**: Signed audit opinion

## Regulatory Change Management

### Monitoring Process
1. **Track**: Subscribe to regulatory updates (tax authorities, SEC, FASB, IASB)
2. **Assess**: Evaluate impact on the company's operations and reporting
3. **Plan**: Develop implementation plan for changes
4. **Execute**: Update policies, processes, and systems
5. **Review**: Verify implementation and effectiveness

documents.title: Budgeting & Forecasting
documents.summary: Standards and process for annual budgeting, quarterly forecasting, and financial planning
documents.body:
# Budgeting & Forecasting

## Overview

This document defines the budgeting and forecasting process. The goal is to produce accurate, actionable financial plans that guide decision-making and resource allocation.

## Annual Budget Cycle

### Timeline
| Phase | Timing | Owner | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strategic planning | Jul-Aug | Executive team | Set company goals, priorities, and high-level targets |
| Department submissions | Sep | Department heads | Submit budget requests with justifications |
| Finance review | Oct | Finance team | Consolidate, challenge assumptions, identify gaps |
| Executive review | Nov | Executive team | Review consolidated budget, make trade-off decisions |
| Board approval | Dec | Board of Directors | Final approval of annual budget |
| Implementation | Jan | All departments | Budget loaded into financial systems |

### Budget Components

**Revenue Budget:**
- By product/service line
- By sales channel
- By customer segment
- Assumptions: growth rate, churn rate, pricing changes, new product launches

**Operating Expense Budget:**
- **Personnel**: Salaries, benefits, bonuses, commissions, payroll taxes
- **Sales & Marketing**: Advertising, events, content, tools, agency fees
- **R&D**: Engineering salaries, cloud infrastructure, software licenses, R&D tax credits
- **G&A**: Legal, accounting, insurance, office/rent, travel, software subscriptions

**Capital Expenditure Budget:**
- Equipment and hardware
- Software and technology investments
- Facility improvements

## Forecasting Process

### Rolling Forecast
- **12-month rolling forecast**: Updated quarterly
- **Current quarter**: Updated monthly
- **Forecast horizon**: Rolling 12 months (not tied to fiscal year)

### Forecast Methods

| Method | When to Use | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Bottom-up | Department-level expenses | Each department builds forecast from specific drivers |
| Top-down | Revenue | Start with market size, apply market share, growth rates |
| Driver-based | Variable costs | Model expenses based on key volume drivers |
| Zero-based | Discretionary spending | Every expense must be justified from zero |
| Statistical | Stable, predictable lines | Use time-series models for consistent patterns |

### Variance Analysis Process
- **Monthly**: Review actuals vs forecast. Investigate variances > 10%.
- **Quarterly**: Full forecast refresh. Update assumptions based on YTD actuals.
- **Trigger-based**: Re-forecast when a material event occurs.

## Financial Modeling Standards

### Model Structure
- **Inputs tab**: All assumptions in one place, clearly labeled
- **Calculations tab**: Transparent calculations (avoid hard-coding)
- **Outputs tab**: Summary financial statements and KPIs
- **Dashboard tab**: Key metrics visualization

### Best Practices
- One row = one assumption
- Color coding: Blue = hard-coded input, Black = formula, Green = reference
- Include data validation and error checks
- Version control: Save dated versions
- Document assumptions: Add comments to key cells

### Required Scenarios
| Scenario | Description |
|---|---|
| Base case | Most likely outcome |
| Upside | Optimistic assumptions (e.g., +20% revenue) |
| Downside | Conservative assumptions (e.g., -20% revenue) |
| Pessimistic | Minimum viable scenario (survival) |

## Budget vs Actual Reporting

### Monthly BvA Report
For each department and line item:
| Line Item | Budget | Actual | Variance $ | Variance % | Explanation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Personnel | $500K | $485K | ($15K) | -3% | Open headcount not filled |
| Marketing | $200K | $234K | $34K | 17% | Additional ad spend for product launch |

### Required Explanations
- Variance > 10% AND > $10K: Written explanation required
- Favorable variance: Explain why under budget (savings or timing?)
- Unfavorable variance: Explain root cause and corrective action

documents.title: Internal Audit & Risk Management
documents.summary: Internal audit procedures, risk assessment framework, and risk mitigation strategies
documents.body:
# Internal Audit & Risk Management

## Overview

Internal audit provides independent assurance that the company's risk management, control, and governance processes are operating effectively. This document defines the audit methodology and risk management framework.

## Risk Management Framework

### Risk Categories

| Category | Examples | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| **Strategic** | Competitive pressure, market shifts, M&A integration | Executive team |
| **Operational** | Process failures, system outages, supply chain disruption | Department heads |
| **Financial** | Liquidity risk, credit risk, FX risk, interest rate risk | CFO / Treasurer |
| **Compliance** | Regulatory changes, contractual breaches, data privacy | Legal / Compliance |
| **Reputational** | Brand damage, negative press, social media backlash | Communications |
| **Technology** | Cybersecurity, data loss, system availability | CTO / CISO |
| **Legal** | Litigation, intellectual property, contract disputes | General Counsel |

### Risk Assessment Process

1. **Identify**: Catalog risks across all categories
2. **Assess**: Score each risk on likelihood (1-5) and impact (1-5)
3. **Prioritize**: Risk score = Likelihood x Impact (max 25)
4. **Respond**: Determine mitigation strategy
5. **Monitor**: Track risk status and mitigation progress
6. **Report**: Update risk register quarterly

### Risk Response Strategies

| Strategy | When to Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Avoid** | Risk outweighs potential benefit | Don't enter a high-risk market |
| **Reduce** | Can mitigate without eliminating | Implement additional controls |
| **Transfer** | Another party can absorb the risk | Purchase insurance, use hedging |
| **Accept** | Low likelihood/impact, or cost exceeds benefit | Self-insure small losses |
| **Share** | Partner to distribute the risk | Joint venture, partnership |

## Internal Audit Methodology

### Audit Types

| Type | Frequency | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Financial audit | Annual | Internal controls over financial reporting |
| Operational audit | Every 2-3 years | Process efficiency and effectiveness |
| Compliance audit | Annual | Adherence to regulations and policies |
| IT audit | Annual | IT general controls, cybersecurity |
| Fraud investigation | As needed | Suspicious activity or whistleblower reports |

### Audit Process

1. **Risk Assessment** (Annual): Identify auditable entities, assess inherent risk, develop audit plan
2. **Planning**: Define scope, objectives, methodology, and timeline
3. **Fieldwork**: Document processes, test controls, gather evidence
4. **Findings**: Document issues, root causes, and recommendations
5. **Reporting**: Draft report, discuss with management, issue final report
6. **Remediation Tracking**: Monitor corrective actions to completion

## Whistleblower Program

### Reporting Channels
- **Hotline**: Third-party operated, anonymous
- **Email**: ethics@company.com
- **Direct**: Chief Compliance Officer or Audit Committee Chair

### Protection Policy
- Zero tolerance for retaliation against good-faith reporters
- Reports can be anonymous where legally permitted
- All reports are investigated promptly and confidentially
- Annual training on whistleblower rights and protections

## Risk Register Template

| # | Risk | Category | Likelihood | Impact | Score | Mitigation | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Data breach | Technology | 3 | 5 | 15 | SOC 2 certification, EDR, employee training | CISO | Active |
| 2 | Revenue shortfall | Strategic | 3 | 4 | 12 | Diversified revenue streams, pipeline management | VP Sales | Monitoring |
| 3 | Regulatory change (tax) | Compliance | 2 | 4 | 8 | Subscribe to regulatory alerts, annual tax review | Tax Director | Active |
| 4 | Key person dependency | Operational | 3 | 3 | 9 | Cross-training, documentation, succession planning | HR | Mitigating |

documents.title: Accounts Payable & Receivable Procedures
documents.summary: Standard operating procedures for accounts payable and receivable processes
documents.body:
# Accounts Payable & Receivable Procedures

## Overview

This document defines the standard operating procedures for Accounts Payable (AP) and Accounts Receivable (AR). These procedures ensure accurate, timely, and controlled processing of all payments and collections.

## Accounts Payable (AP)

### Vendor Onboarding
1. **Vendor request**: Department submits new vendor request with W-9/W-8BEN
2. **Due diligence**: Verify tax ID, bank details, business license
3. **Approval**: Manager approves vendor setup
4. **Creation**: AP creates vendor record in ERP system
5. **Notification**: Vendor notified of setup and payment terms

### Invoice Processing

**Receipt:**
- All invoices sent to ap@company.com
- AP logs receipt with date and invoice number
- Auto-routed to approver based on department/GL coding

**Three-Way Match:**
For purchase order (PO) invoices:
1. **PO**: Verify PO exists, has budget, and is approved
2. **Receipt**: Verify goods/services received (receiving report)
3. **Invoice**: Verify invoice matches PO and receipt

**Non-PO Invoices:**
- Requires manager approval
- Must include original receipt or service documentation

### Payment Run Schedule

| Run Type | Frequency | Processing Day | Payment Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard (NET 30) | Weekly | Monday | Friday same week |
| Rush (NET 15) | Bi-weekly | Wednesday | Following Wednesday |
| Wire/ACH | Daily (by 2 PM) | Same day | Same day |
| International | Weekly | Tuesday | 3-5 business days |

### Payment Methods

| Method | Threshold | Processing Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACH | Any | 1-2 business days | Preferred method |
| Check | Any | 3-5 business days | Include remittance advice |
| Wire (domestic) | > $10K | Same day | Requires CFO approval |
| Wire (international) | > $5K | 3-5 days | Requires FX rate approval |

### Early Payment Discounts
- 2/10 Net 30: Take 2% discount if paid within 10 days
- Evaluate discount ROI: 2% for 20 days early = ~36% annualized
- Always take discount if cash position allows

## Accounts Receivable (AR)

### Invoicing Process

**Standard Invoicing (Subscription/Recurring):**
- Auto-generated on billing date
- Sent via automated billing system (Stripe, Chargebee, etc.)
- Customer receives invoice + receipt by email
- Recognized in AR immediately

**Manual Invoicing:**
- Created for non-standard billing (professional services, one-time fees)
- Requires approved contract or work order
- Sent within 1 business day of billing trigger

### Collections Process

| Aging Bucket | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Current | No action (standard) | - |
| 1-30 days past due | Send reminder email (automated) | AR system |
| 31-60 days past due | Email + phone call from AR team | AR specialist |
| 61-90 days past due | Escalated to AR manager. Payment plan offered. | AR manager |
| 91+ days past due | Final notice. Sent to collections or legal. | CFO / Legal |

### Cash Application

**Automatic:**
- Payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal) auto-match payments to invoices
- ACH payments matched via reference number
- Exception rate: < 2%

**Manual:**
- Check receipts: Apply within 1 business day
- Wire transfers: Apply within 2 hours of receipt notification
- Unidentified payments: Research within 24 hours

### AR Reporting

| Report | Frequency | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| AR Aging Summary | Daily | AR specialist |
| DSO Calculation | Weekly | AR manager |
| Collections Forecast | Weekly | AR manager |
| Bad Debt Reserve Analysis | Monthly | Controller |

### Bad Debt Management

- **Reserve methodology**: % of aging buckets (current: 1%, 31-60: 10%, 61-90: 25%, 91+: 50%, 180+: 100%)
- **Write-off**: Requires CFO approval for amounts > $1,000
- **Recovery**: Written-off accounts pursued by collections agency (50% recovery target)
- **Reactivation**: If customer pays after write-off, reverse write-off and recognize payment
